title: The Player Involvement Model
role: CENTRAL CHAPTER — the load-bearing theoretical chapter of the volume. Introduces the 6-dimensional Player Involvement Model (kinesthetic, spatial, shared, narrative, affective, ludic) cross-cut by a 2-phase temporal distinction (macro = off-line involvement; micro = moment-to-moment in-session involvement). Establishes the three-tier attentional hierarchy (attention → involvement → presence/immersion). Articulates the grounded-theoretic, qualitative-interview methodology distilling 3 years of WoW + Planetside research. Closes with the volume's strongest negative-definitional move: a sustained excision of the 'magic circle' (Huizinga via Salen+Zimmerman, Juul, Suits) and the 'fun' essentialism from the operational vocabulary of the model.

expected_dimension_definitions_present.ch3_definition_paraphrase_seed: Avatar / game-piece control in virtual environments, from learning controls to fluency of internalized movement; foregrounded when controls 'make themselves present' (un-mastered or demand complex sequences). Full development deferred to Ch.4.

Engagement with the spatial qualities of a virtual environment via spatial control, navigation, and exploration; the process of internalizing game spaces such that the player senses inhabiting a place rather than perceiving a representation of space. Full development deferred to Ch.5.
Engagement from awareness of and interaction with other agents (human- or computer-controlled) in the game environment — cohabitation, cooperation, competition. Full development deferred to Ch.6.
Engagement with story elements scripted into the game and with story elements emergent from player interaction (the alterbiography concept). Full development deferred to Ch.7.

Emotional engagement ranging from calming aesthetic-scene response, to adrenaline-rush of competitive FPS rounds, to the uncanny of action-horror; the rhetorical strategies of affect designed into the game and those precipitated by the player's interpretation. Full development deferred to Ch.8.

Engagement with choices made in the game and their repercussions; goals stipulated by the game, by the player, or by the player community; importance of opportunity cost. Full development deferred to Ch.9.

macro_phase.definition_paraphrase_seed: Off-line involvement — pregame and postgame thinking, planning, community participation, anticipation, motivation to return to the game; the longer-term contextualization of the moment of gameplay. Corroborated by Poels et al. 2010 'postgame experiences' focus-group study.

micro_phase.definition_paraphrase_seed: Moment-to-moment, in-session engagement during gameplay; ergodically active (in the dispositional, readiness-to-act sense, not merely the physical-input sense); attentionally structured by the same six dimensions but operating on a finer temporal grain.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.pipeline: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy (BCAP)
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Calleja's macro/micro temporal-phase distinction (the chapter's signature theoretical move) is the strongest pre-augmentation bridge in the entire volume to phenomenological time-analysis. Macro = anticipatory + retentional structure of player-being-toward-the-game; micro = ekstatic moment-to-moment engagement. BCAP's analyses of kairos and ekstatic temporality would deepen Calleja's relatively undertheorized temporal phenomenology. ANTICIPATORY.

Bridge from Ch.3's micro-phase temporality (and the ergodicity-as-readiness-to-act notion of dispositional action) to aisthesis-kinesis and Aristotelian continuous-motion analysis. The 'readiness to act' formulation reads almost as a sketch of dunamis/hexis without the vocabulary. ANTICIPATORY.

Ch.3 IS the dissertation's analytical instrument. The 6 dimensions x 2 phases grid is the operationalization spine; the 'three-tier hierarchy (attention -> involvement -> presence/immersion)' is the dissertation's import-ready stratification; the qualitative grounded-theoretic methodology supplies the empirical-adaptation template. Every Ch.3 concept is a candidate dissertation-deployable construct.

Per-dimension pentad mapping anchors here in Ch.3 since this is where each dimension is first defined. Provisional projected mappings: Kinesthetic->Agency; Spatial->Scene; Shared->Agent (+ratios); Narrative->Act+Purpose; Affective->Attitude; Ludic->Purpose+Act. Burke is wholly ABSENT from Calleja's text per Phase 0 cite-check — entirely creative augmentation.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.pipeline: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Per-dimension Uexkullian-construct mapping anchors here in Ch.3. Provisional projected mappings: Kinesthetic <-> Funktionskreis (the perception-action loop); Spatial <-> Umwelt + Merkwelt/Wirkwelt; Affective <-> Merktone/Wirktone. Singly anchored (the Gibson-mediation hypothesis is falsified per Phase 0).

The 'internalization' move (kinesthetic controls passing from conscious-attentional to internalized-automatic; Ch.3 p.45) parallels habituation-of-phantasia operations; the 'layered + transparent' structure of the dimensions resembles imagistic-overlay phenomena described in rhetorical-vision and deliberative-phantasia literatures. ANTICIPATORY — Calleja never uses 'phantasia' or any cognate.

expected_tensions: Anti-essentialist Wittgensteinian definitional posture vs. construction of a six-dimensional model that taxonomically organizes player experience (tension carried over from Ch.1, made operationally explicit in Ch.3's 'Structure of the Model').

Bottom-up grounded-theoretic dimension-derivation (clusters emerge from interview data, p.37) vs. top-down theoretical framing (the 6 dimensions are presented as exhaustive even though the empirical base is two MMOGs).

Macro vs. micro phase asymmetry: macro-phase exposition is one section (pp.38-40); micro-phase is the chapter's analytic center of gravity and dominates Chs.4-9. The model is more developed micro-side than macro-side at the moment of its own introduction.

Excision of magic-circle / lusory-attitude / fun (pp.46-53) creates negative-definitional pressure on the model: the model's identity is partly constituted by what it refuses (Huizinga, Suits, the 'games are fun' tradition). The chapter must do both positive-constructive work (defining 6 dimensions + 2 phases) and negative-purgative work (clearing the magic-circle apparatus) in 20 pages.
